target.title: fix(ai): keep OpenAI tool call id truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`normalizeToolCallId` in `openai-completions.ts:1053` truncates oversized OpenAI tool call IDs with `id.slice(0, 40)`. When a tool call ID contains a UTF-16 surrogate pair straddling positions 39-40, `slice` splits the pair and leaves an unpaired high surrogate — producing invalid Unicode in the outbound API request.

## Why This Change Was Made

`String.prototype.slice(0, 40)` operates on UTF-16 code units. A surrogate pair (e.g. 🐱 `\uD83D\uDC31`) consumes 2 code units. The fix switches to `truncateUtf16Safe(id, 40)` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, an existing repo helper used by sibling UTF-16 PRs (#104054, #107664, #109561, #109498, #109839).

Sibling surfaces (non-OpenAI provider paths, other `normalizeToolCallId` branches) are unaffected — the change is scoped to the `model.provider === "openai"` check at line 1053.

Collision check: searched open PRs; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- Multi-model `openai` provider tool-call conversations produce valid Unicode in all IDs
- No change for IDs without surrogate pairs at the 40-unit boundary
- Non-OpenAI provider paths unchanged

## Evidence

Exact head: `e1b14f5ac5caf63be69465d970f56b8582bd6cf7`

### Format and diff check

```
$ git diff --check origin/main..HEAD && echo ok
ok
```

### Vitest suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  47 passed (47)
```

Test `"truncates an oversized tool call id without cutting a surrogate pair"`:
- Input: 41-code-unit tool call ID with 🐱 surrogate pair at positions 39-40
- Mock response allows the stream to flow through `client.chat.completions.create` — the actual API-call boundary
- Normalized `tool_call_id` verified in `mockOpenAIOptionsRef.payloads[0]` — the exact params sent over the network
- `stopReason === "stop"` — stream completes naturally
- Verified: 39 code units, clean ASCII (surrogate pair dropped safely), no unpaired surrogate

### Real behavior proof — terminal run against production import

The proof script imports the exact same `truncateUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice` used by the production code at `openai-completions.ts:1053`, and calls it with a 41-code-unit tool call ID (39 ASCII + 🐱 at [39,40]).

```
$ node --import tsx proof-openai-tool-call-id-utf16-truncation.mts
node=v24.18.0
head=e1b14f5ac5caf63be69465d970f56b8582bd6cf7
id_length=41 (39 ASCII + 🐱 @ [39,40])

Before fix (raw .slice(0, 40)):
{"length":40,"last_code_unit":"0xd83d","trailing_surrogate":true}

After fix (truncateUtf16Safe(id, 40)):
{"length":39,"last_char_code":"0x61","trailing_surrogate":false,"prefix_preserved":true}
  ok: site1: raw .slice(0,40) leaves unpaired high surrogate
  ok: site1: truncateUtf16Safe(id,40) has no trailing surrogate
  ok: site1: truncateUtf16Safe(id,40) preserves prefix
  ok: site1: truncateUtf16Safe(id,40) result <= 40 code units
  ok: ascii: truncateUtf16Safe matches .slice for plain text
  ok: short: truncateUtf16Safe returns short id unchanged

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 6 passed, 0 failed
```

Before fix: `trailing_surrogate: true` — the outbound API payload would contain an unpaired `U+D83D`.
After fix: `trailing_surrogate: false` — valid UTF-16, 39 code units, prefix preserved.

### Mutation check

Revert `truncateUtf16Safe(id, 40)` → `id.slice(0, 40)` in openai-completions.ts:1053:

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/ai/src/providers/openai-completions.test.ts -t "truncates an oversized"

 FAIL  ... > truncates an oversized tool call id without cutting a surrogate pair
AssertionError: expected true to be false

 Tests  1 failed | 46 skipped (47)
```

Restore `truncateUtf16Safe(id, 40)` → 47/47 passed.

### Not tested

- Live OpenAI API roundtrip with real API key (covered by `mockOpenAIOptionsRef.payloads[0]` at the network-call boundary)
- Non-OpenAI provider tool call ID truncation paths (unchanged)
- Tool call IDs with multi-codepoint grapheme clusters at the boundary
